basic_info.title: RLOMM: An Efficient and Robust Online Map Matching Framework with Reinforcement Learning
basic_info.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Management of Data (PACMMOD), Vol. 3, No. 3 (SIGMOD), Article 209, June 2025; preprint arXiv:2502.06825 (accepted by SIGMOD 2025)

gap_analysis.whats_missing: RLOMM casts ONLINE map matching as an Online Markov Decision Process solved with RL, but its policy selects among candidate road segments using a comprehensive, hand-designed reward function (distance/transition/future-oriented terms) rather than acting inside a learned latent world model. It uses GNN + recurrent (RNN) encoders for road and trajectory plus contrastive learning to align them in latent space, but the RL decisions are over explicit candidate-segment states, not over a transformer-encoded latent representation; it relies on ground-truth matched paths for training/evaluation rather than being label-free; and it has no RDF/KG semantic enrichment or a transformer encoder.
gap_analysis.novelty_reasoning: It shares the sequential-decision-RL framing and trajectory-road latent alignment of the thesis, but uses GNN+RNN (not a semantic transformer), a hand-crafted reward over explicit candidates (not latent-world-model RL), and supervised ground-truth matches, so none of the three pillars is fully covered.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Most direct precedent for treating fleet-GPS map matching as a sequential RL decision process at scale, making it the closest baseline on the RL axis for BMW Foresight fleet-trajectory analytics, though it is online and supervised rather than offline latent-world-model and label-free.
